items.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016
items.q: And then of course there was always Bill Evans.

ctx.x: Definitely. Definitely. Again, when I was at the age where you think about how you want to play, I had four musicians at the generation of McCoy. It was Herbie Hancock, it was McCoy Tyner, it was Chick Corea and it was Keith Jarrett. And then of course there was always Bill Evans. But I wanted to mix those four guys — I don’t mean strictly, but that was kind of deliberate. Those were my four most important.
Oh here’s an odd one: Bent Fabric.
